BMW's First Large Minivan Wants a Piece of the North American Sliding-Door MPV Sector – Rendering
7 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The Bavarian automaker BMW just kicked off production of its first-ever US-made all-electric model – Plant Spartanburg and the Woodruff nearby location now make the US’s first electric SUV from BMW, all thanks to a $1.7 billion investment to make the all-new, first-ever BMW iX5 feel right at home in North America.
The largest premium automaker in the world dares to take a leap of faith at a time when the US automotive market isn’t in love with EVs anymore but with hybrids. Alas, they probably don’t worry much, as the iX5 will be shipped all around the world, plus they have a long list of novelties coming out next year to make sure they cover all customer needs.
There’s a new BMW i1 coming as the entry-level EV , fresh X1 and iX1 subcompact crossover SUVs, updated X2 and iX2 models, the practical i3 Touring, the first-ever all-electric M3 plus an iX3 M along with an iX4 M, and also the major Neue Klasse redesign of the 5 Series and M5, plus the upcoming all-new X7 and iX7 along with the BMW Alpina 7 flagships .
Quite obviously, there will be something for everyone – both ICE and EV along with PHEV in between them. Alas, there’s one person who thinks that BMW still has room for one more new vehicle in the roster. He’s a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators, and he stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI for this – their latest unofficial, hypothetical design project.
Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on something different for BMW – a large Neue Klasse minivan. This model could attack the large Mercedes-Benz MPV, the all-new and all-electric VLE – which is the primary target from the standpoint of the pixel master.
As such, it would provide an exotic alternative to the VLE , which features two powertrain versions – a front-motor FWD version, VLE 300, and the dual-motor AWD VLE 400 4Matic, packing 271 or 415 hp and a 115-kWh battery pack on an 800-volt architecture with up to 678 km (421 miles) of range. The rivaling BMW minivan could share the fresh Neue Klasse architecture with the i3 and iX3, rocking their RWD and dual-motor AWD powertrains with up to 463 horsepower and comparable range.
But on the other hand, we’d really like this quirky minivan to also come to North America, where it could provide an interesting alternative to the likes of Chrysler Pacifica, Toyota Sienna, Honda Odyssey, and the Kia Carnival. It would need an ICE or hybrid powertrain, though, as Americans aren’t fond of EVs too much these days. Cool or not? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)

Virtually Reborn Ford Thunderbird Super Coupe Steals the CGI Soul of a Mighty Aston Martin Valen
7 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
The Ford Motor Company has been pretty busy lately – Ford Racing has a new Global Director, the Blue Oval is now in the battery business, launched the Ford Custom Garage Maverick SV300T package, and also introduced us to the Mustang GTD 1901, which pays tribute to Henry Ford’s original race car.
Ford Racing’s new Global Director is Pascal Zurlinden, as the subsidiary “grows into a broader global business, connecting what it learns in competition to the vehicles and experiences it creates for customers.” The Blue Oval has also joined the battery-making business, with cells coming off the line at the BlueOval Battery Park Michigan in Marshall as they go to the Louisville plant to enter the packs of the new Ford Fathom EV pickup truck.
As far as the model novelties are concerned, Ford Custom Garage launched the limited-edition SV300T package recently in two configurations – Black or Bronze – bringing both Ford Accessories and Ford Racing Parts together on the 2025 and 2026 Maverick XLT, Lariat, and Lobo models packing the 2.0-liter EcoBoost engine and all-wheel drive, now rocking 300 horsepower under the hood.
While all fans wait for the Ford Mustang GTD Competition upgrade, the Ford Motor Company actually introduced the 2028 model year Mustang GTD with the 1901 livery , which pays its respects to Henry Ford’s first 1901 two-cylinder race car. The company itself wasn’t even founded back then, so Ford Racing is technically older (125 years) than its parent enterprise.
As such, with all the commotion around the Blue Oval, we’re not surprised that the rumor mill and the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators are keeping an eye on everything Ford. Just recently, someone stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to focus on a fresh Ford. Or an Aston Martin. Or both…
More precisely, Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm and dreams of a FoMoCo idea – again. He recently crafted things like the rumored, upcoming S650 Ford Mustang Cobra, a return of the Crown Victoria sedan, and even a Mercury Cougar XR7 along with a Ford Taurus SHO.
But now he’s taking the unofficial, hypothetical design projects to new heights – up there on cloud number nine alongside ultra-luxury and exotic creations like the recent Aston Martin Valen. The latter is a new grand tourer by the British automaker that’s powered by a 5.2-liter AE31 twin-turbo V12 shared with the third-generation Vanquish, rocking for this application no less than 838 hp (625 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,001 Nm) of torque.
Alas, the pixel master sees its front end as quite similar to the shape of the fascia of 1960s Ford T-Birds, which is why he decided to CGI mash the Valen with the Ford aura to attempt to create a fresh Thunderbird Super Coupe. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jim (@jlord8)

Mansory Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 Is So Brown It Should Come With a Giant Waste Bag
19 photos
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory
It is usually the Maybach version of the Mercedes GLS that gets the spotlight in our news feed, but this time, it is all about its sporty sibling from the Affalterbach division. That would be the Mercedes-AMG GLS 63, by the way.
This particular full-size SUV has come directly from Mansory’s portfolio, and given the overall look, we wouldn’t have expected it to have been signed by a different tuner to be honest. That’s because it is definitely on the controversial side of things, as the color choice makes it look questionable, to say the least, and the extras on the outside are not exactly head-turning for the reasons either, are they?
Nevertheless, beauty is indeed in the eyes of the beholder as they say, and while some may find this tuned Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 debatable, others would say that it is the absolute bomb, and if the latter category’s pockets are deep enough, then they would probably ask where they should sign, and how much does this thing cost. And guess what? It is not for sale. Mansory said this is a bespoke project, and it is likely a special commission.
The images you see in the gallery were recently shared by the tuner’s founder on social media, and they reveal the ride in question from multiple angles. This particular machine features a new grille at the front, with extra vents and some additional lights on the sides, as well as the tuner’s logo in the middle. Further down, we can clearly see that there are new bumper add-ons, including those around the side vents, and the ever-present splitter, which features blades on the sides in this case.
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory Moreover, the pictured Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 also comes with an entirely new hood that has gone down the vented route. There is also new trim on the front fenders, and we can also see that the side steps appear to be new as well. The fender flares are part of the makeover, and so are the door mirror casings. Out back, the ride sports some add-ons on the sides of the bumper, a new roof-mounted spoiler, a fresh diffuser with an extra brake light in the middle, and new logos on the tailgate.
Some of the components mentioned above features a (forged-like) brown look, and the wheels, which are quite familiar, as the tuner has used them on numerous other projects recently, feature a bronze-like finish, and measure 24 inches in diameter. It seems that the SUV in question hasn’t had its suspension modified in any way, but you may want to refrain from quoting us on that for obvious reasons.
Don’t go anywhere yet, because we also have to put the spotlight on the interior. That’s because this Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 features custom leather upholstery that mixes black and brown. There are some very special inserts, including those on the seatbacks, and the Mansory emblems are ever present. The dashboard, center console, and door card trim is also new, and so is the steering wheel. A starry sky headliner is part of the makeover, as you can see in the pictures shared in our gallery.
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory Could a power boost be part of the makeover? Well, it certainly could, because Mansory tends to apply plenty of elbow grease to most of its projects. However, given that this aspect hasn’t been mentioned at all in the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page, we cannot tell you for sure whether this machine boasts more oomph or not. Our bet would be on the yes part, though that’s our two cents.
Even without any outside intervention whatsoever, the Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 is still very agile for a full-size SVU, taking 4.1 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill. Powering it is the ubiquitous 4.0-liter bi-turbo V8 engine, which is officially good for 603 hp (612 ps/450 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque.
The output and thrust has been retained in the facelifted iteration, which will go on sale soon in the United States of America. And that’s despite the fact that this model, as well as its smaller sibling, the GLE from AMG, benefit from a new integrated starter generator and a 48-volt mild-hybrid system, adding 23 hp (23 ps/17 kW) and 151 lb-ft (205 Nm) of torque. Both get the latest AMG Speedshift TCT 9-speed automatic transmission, channeling the power to the 4Matic+ AWD system with variable torque distribution.
Pricing will be released in due course, but the pre-facelifted iteration, which is what the pictured Mercedes- AMG GLS 63 is, kicked off at $151,050. Nonetheless, reports indicate that it should start at $155,250, before destination. But that does not matter in this story, as what does is whether you like the tuned machine or not. So, do you? For what it’s worth, I definitely don’t, but then again, I am not exactly a Mansory fan either. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kourosh Mansory (@_kourosh_mansory)
